review_text_raw:
Cannot really say recommend or not - to me it is a 5/10 game. Overall, it is not quite like a hacking game but more like a chess game. So if you like it - good worth a try. If you are expecting something similar to other hacking games or richer experience - not really your choice.

Played it for two times with the realtime and default modes. Realtime mode is more fun to me as I don't need to wait for the steps ending. The flow of playing is more smooth. 

Good part: UI and music are good. Story line of the first half goes really well with many side stories to enrich the characters. [spoiler] Like the idea of angel vs evil choices.[/spoiler] 

Bad part: After [spoiler]introducing the ices and trackers[/spoiler], the game starts to get boring although the difficulty level is increasing - it starts to be the same core [spoiler]playing with just more ices, more tracking techniques, less time/steps[/spoiler]. Story is good before [spoiler]signal reports you to Snail and Clover - and then the story goes quickly with your choice with much confusion. [/spoiler] For multi-language players, there is a bug that the information downloaded from data nodes shrink to a level that you cannot read. It is annoying so I finally played with English in the end.

review_text_raw:
Given its a hacking strategy game I super do not agree or enjoy:
- You never see your enemy, you trip into them or guess where they might be (and suffer if your wrong)
- You cannot re-plan missions
- You are not provided enough information ahead of time to know which programs to take along

If these terrible design decisions had been mitigated or provided as optional, we'd have a great game here. I guess the intent is you are to go in with your wits and the tools you have and hope for the best but without any real agency, your just tripping through landmines. Failing forward isn't very fun; it sounds a lot like life.

Wow this is wild

- You literally cannot see ICE before running into them or rolling the dice and using sniffer (maybe your right, maybe your wrong, but you can't use it again for a bit)
- It is in no way obvious that I can restart a mission; I learned outside of the game that I can restart a mission while in the mission but I cannot re-plan (choose better set of programs), which is what I said
- SOME network details are given in advance, not everything as I'd like; how do I reroll and try again?

Look your game isn't for me. I'm not lying or making things up, I have no reason to, the design choices aren't very good from my point of view.

review_text_raw: Just a big buggy waste of time, nothing special here. The strategy gameplay is very limited and the "story" in between each mission is frustrating to navigate how to unlock the next mission. Also technical issues such as bugs that softlock forcing a restart, and audio coming through even though master volume is set to 0. [strike]The "Finish Act 1" achievement is less than 10% of players which shows the retention of interest here[/strike] without going into detail about the positives and negatives of this game.
